CustomerSync.// RunAtTimeUtc: Daily run time in UTC, HH:mm format (e.g. '01:00' for 01:00 UTC). Leave empty to disable the scheduled run; the dev-only manual trigger endpoint still works regardless.

AppAccess.// GroupId: Object id of the Entra access group, read DIRECTLY (GET /groups/{id}/...). The managed identity's group read is scoped to specific groups — it cannot list/search groups — so the id must be configured for deployed environments. EMPTY here ON PURPOSE: the base default fails open (unfiltered, diagnostic reports NotConfigured) so no environment can ever filter by the wrong group. Each env sets its OWN group in appsettings.{Env}.json — Development/Dev use the dev group, QA/Production use theirs. Once an env's GroupId is set AND its managed identity has the scoped-group read + User.ReadBasic.All grant, filtering activates automatically (no redeploy — the grant is AAD-side; cache refreshes within ~CacheMinutes).
AppAccess.// GroupName: Display label for the diagnostic, and the resolve-by-name fallback when GroupId is empty (name search only works under a developer credential locally — never as the scoped managed identity).
AppAccess.// CacheMinutes: How long a successful membership read is cached before Graph is asked again (failures are retried after ~5 minutes).

Ctrm.// Source: Which data source backs contract and ticket reads: 'ods' (or EMPTY) keeps every read on the ODS views exactly as before; 'ctrm' routes them at the Scoular.GraphQL API. EMPTY here ON PURPOSE so no environment can accidentally leave ODS - each env opts in via appsettings.{Env}.json. On 'ctrm' every contract and ticket read is CTRM: per-producer live, trade-unit-wide (Build-a-List, Actionable Insights, crop-year dashboard) via a cached producer-set read that mirrors the ODS flow (trade units -> producers in Origination -> CTRM). Only GetPricingLinesAsync (unused by the UI), farm and source-id lookups still delegate to ODS.
Ctrm.// GraphQlUri: Full URL of the GraphQL endpoint, e.g. https://apiqa.scoular.com/internal/graphql. Empty disables the CTRM path regardless of Source.
Ctrm.// TenantId: Entra tenant for the client-credentials token. Same tenant as AzureAd above.
Ctrm.// ClientId: App registration id used to call the CTRM API (client-credentials flow).
Ctrm.// Audience: Scope requested for the token, e.g. api://<api-app-id>/.default
Ctrm.// ClientSecret: NEVER set here. Supplied from Key Vault as secret 'Ctrm--ClientSecret' (Key Vault maps '--' to ':'), or omit entirely once the managed identity holds an app role on the CTRM API.
Ctrm.// PageSize: Rows per page when filling the contract snapshot. 500 is the API's observed ceiling; values above it are clamped.
Ctrm.// PageConcurrency: How many contract pages are fetched at once. Page 1 is fetched alone for its totalCount, which tells us the page count and frees the rest to run in parallel. A 500-row page with pricing lines costs ~10s, so this is the difference between a ~195s and a ~50s warm-up. Clamped to 1-8: a 429 from APIM fails the whole snapshot, so headroom matters more than the last few seconds.
Ctrm.// LiveCacheSeconds: How long a live per-producer read is reused. Selecting a producer triggers the contract list, the pricing lines and the pacing card, which all want the same rows — this coalesces them into ONE CTRM call. Keep it small (seconds): it exists to avoid duplicate round trips, not to cache data. Set 0 to disable.
Ctrm.// TradeUnitContractStrategy: How the trade-unit-wide contract read (Build-a-List, Insights, crop-year) fetches a producer set's full history. 'perProducer' (default): one indexed contracts(customerId:) call per producer, fanned out at TradeUnitPerProducerConcurrency - measured 2026-08-27 on QA at avg 1.5s per call, 48 producers in 23s, no errors; ~2 minutes cold for a 587-producer trade unit, then cached. 'customerIds': the chunked list filter - the right shape once the API owner fixes its plan, but today every page is a ~25s server-side scan that trips the server's own 30s limit under any concurrent load and never completed for that same trade unit. Flip to 'customerIds' only after a probe shows a 500-code page under ~5s cold.
Ctrm.// TradeUnitPerProducerConcurrency: Upper bound on concurrent per-producer calls in the perProducer strategy, applied BEFORE TradeUnitMaxConcurrentRequests - so the effective parallelism is the smaller of the two. Kept as a separate dial so this strategy can be tuned without touching the shared background cap. Raising it past the shared cap has no effect.
Ctrm.// TradeUnitCacheMinutes: How long the trade-unit-wide CONTRACT read (contracts(customerIds:) full history for the producers in the selected trade units) is reused before it is refreshed. Refreshes never block: an expired entry is served to the caller while the refresh runs behind it, so this is how far behind CTRM a prompt can be, not how long anyone waits. Each refresh is a ~25s server-side scan per page (measured cold: 500 codes 24.7s), so keep this in tens of minutes - a 5-minute cadence per active trade-unit set was too much background load.
Ctrm.// TradeUnitContractConcurrency: How many contracts(customerIds:) pages run at once for one trade-unit read. Separate from PageConcurrency on purpose: every one of these pages is a ~25s server-side scan, and five at once alongside a ticket walk starved the server past the 110s client timeout on a 587-producer trade unit (2026-08-27). Two finishes reliably. Raise only after the API owner fixes the list-filter plan.
Ctrm.// TradeUnitMaxConcurrentRequests: Process-wide cap on BACKGROUND CTRM requests in flight at once - the trade-unit contract fan-out and the batched ticket pages, shared across both readers. Interactive per-producer reads (a click on the producer screen) never take a slot, which is the point: without this cap the trade-unit walk saturated the gateway and per-producer reads went from 1-2s to 13-18s (measured 2026-08-27). Raising it speeds the walk and slows clicks; lowering it does the reverse. 6 is the balance: a 587-producer trade unit warms in roughly a minute while clicks stay responsive.
Ctrm.// BackgroundMaxDeferSeconds: How long a background trade-unit request will wait for interactive reads (a producer selection) to finish before going ahead anyway. Background work yields to clicks because they share one gateway: with a walk running, a single producer ticket window measured 5-12s instead of its usual 1-3s (2026-08-27). Bounded so a busy app cannot starve the walk forever - Build-a-List still populates, just more slowly while people are clicking. 0 disables the priority rule and leaves only the concurrency cap.
Ctrm.// ServerTimeoutRetries: How many times a page that CTRM itself timed out (GraphQL error HC0045, "The request exceeded the configured timeout of 00:00:30", returned as HTTP 400) is re-sent. The server finishes the query after answering and caches the result, so the identical request a few seconds later returns in ~1s. A cold contracts(customerIds:) page for 500 producers is 22-25s on a quiet gateway - right at the server limit - so this is what keeps the trade-unit contract read alive under load until the API owner fixes the list-filter plan. Only HC0045 is retried; any other failure returns at once.
Ctrm.// ServerTimeoutRetryDelaySeconds: Pause before each HC0045 re-send, giving the server time to finish and cache. 8s x 4 retries covers a page the server needs up to ~60s to complete.
Ctrm.// TradeUnitContractMaxPagesPerChunk: Page cap (500 rows each) for one 500-producer chunk of the trade-unit-wide contract read. 100 = 50,000 contracts per chunk. The log says TRUNCATED when it is hit.
Ctrm.// TradeUnitTicketMaxPagesPerWindow: Page cap (500 rows each) for one 500-producer chunk of the trade-unit-wide TICKET read within one 366-day window. Per-producer reads keep a fixed cap of 10 because a single producer past 5,000 rows in one window means the filter is not applying; a 500-producer chunk legitimately runs to tens of thousands in the newest window. 200 = 100,000 rows per chunk-window. The log says TRUNCATED when it is hit.
Ctrm.// TicketLookbackDays: How far back the live per-producer ticket read reaches. 1095 = three years, matching the ODS cutoff, because the whole point of the CTRM path is to show the same population ODS does. The server caps a single bill-of-lading range at 366 days, so this is sliced into consecutive windows fetched in parallel and the cost is roughly the slowest window, not the sum: measured warm each window is ~1.0-1.3s, cold up to ~5.5s. Narrowing this is a latency dial that trades away older tickets - a producer's 2024 loads simply stop appearing - so change it deliberately.
Ctrm.// CrossBookedAppliedTickets: Adds a second, contract-scoped ticket read per producer that can see an applied ticket booked entirely under a DIFFERENT customer code. Off by default because it doubles the date scans, and a ticket read is charged by the scan: a producer with no tickets still costs ~3s for a 365-day window, so three years went from three scans to six and dominated a heavy producer's load (13.8s, measured 2026-08-27). The single customerId read still catches split loads on any header the producer appears on at all - only headers with NO detail for the producer are invisible to it, and a 90-producer sample in trade unit 2190 over a full year found zero of those. Turn ON if production data shows applied bushels on the contract disagreeing with the producer's ticket list.
Ctrm.// HistoricalTicketCacheMinutes: How long a ticket WINDOW that ended in the past is reused before it is refetched. The per-producer ticket read is three 366-day windows; the one containing today keeps LiveCacheSeconds because that is where new tickets land, but the two older ones hold tickets that rarely change and cost the most to fetch (~0.8-2.6s each against ~0.3-0.8s for the current year). So a repeat visit within this many minutes pays for the current window only. It is a bound on how stale an OLD ticket's status (a late settlement, a consolidation) can be on screen - not a promise that old tickets never change.
Ctrm.// RecentTicketDays: How far back the recent-unapplied ticket read looks — the one behind Actionable Insights > Spot Loads. 30 matches the cutoff the ODS query used, so leave it there in any environment whose output is being compared against ODS. It is configurable only because 30 days makes the read unverifiable in nonprod: dev CTRM has no ticket activity in the last 30 days for the real producer population (the same ten producers return 0 rows over 30 days and 834 over a year), so Spot Loads renders empty whichever source backs it. Widening this is the only way to prove the path end to end without waiting for data. A wider window is not a data difference — it is a different question.

UsageDashboard.// ExclusionManagers: Short names (UPN before the @) of the IT users allowed to see and manage the usage-dashboard exclusion list. Enforced server-side on the excluded-users/access-users endpoints (on top of AdminOnly); the client hides the gear icon for everyone else. Base list applies to every environment unless overridden in appsettings.{Env}.json.

SecurityHeaders.// SpaConnectSrcHosts: Specific hosts allowed in the SPA CSP connect-src (in addition to 'self' + Microsoft login/graph). Set per environment (appsettings.{Env}.json) to that env's own App Service host — replaces the former *.azurewebsites.net wildcard. Empty here so local dev relies on 'self' + localhost.
